findings.measured: Below 150 Hz the correlation is 0.35; bass and kick may thin out in mono.

steps.text: In Pro-Q, add a low cut at 150 Hz and set that band's stereo placement to Side.

other_options.text: Add a Channel EQ, set Processing to Side, and turn on Low Cut at 150 Hz so the lows are mono.
Check the kick and bass tracks for chorus, wideners or stereo patches.

findings.measured: The audio is still loud at the last sample; the ending may be cut off.

steps.text: In the Bounce window, turn on Include Audio Tail (or extend the cycle range past the last tail).

other_options.text: Set a Fade Out on the last region in the Region inspector, then bounce again.

notes.headline: Two things stand out on this master: the low end is wide enough to thin out in mono, and the file ends at full level as if it was cut off.
notes.summary: Technically this is a solid master at 8.8/10 — true peak sits at -1.06 dBTP, the left/right balance is within 0.06 dB, and overall mono loss is only 0.7 dB. What needs attention is below 150 Hz, where correlation drops to 0.35, so kick and bass are the part most likely to lose weight on a mono system. The other issue is the bounce itself: the audio is still loud at the last sample, so the tail is probably chopped. Fixing both takes the score to 10.

priorities.title: Mono the low end below 150 Hz
priorities.why: With correlation at 0.35 under 150 Hz, kick and bass may thin out on phones, club sub feeds, and anything that sums to mono — the part of the track that carries the weight is the least reliable.

priorities.title: Re-bounce with the tail intact
priorities.why: The file is still at full level on the last sample, so the ending is likely truncated — on release platforms that reads as a hard cut rather than an ending.

listen_for: Flip to mono and listen to the kick and bass together — they should hold their weight, not step back, after the 150 Hz side cut.
In stereo, check that the low cut on the Side band didn't narrow the overall image of the track, only the lows.
Play the last few seconds of the new bounce all the way past the end and confirm the tail decays naturally instead of stopping.
Check the low end on a small speaker or phone, where a wide bass is most likely to disappear.
strengths: True peak at -1.06 dBTP leaves safe margin for lossy encoding.
Left/right balance is essentially centered at 0.06 dB.
Mono loss overall is only 0.7 dB, so the issue is confined to the lows.

judge.priority_order: Both findings are warnings; F1 (wide low end, more likely to affect sub-heavy playback) is placed before F2 (abrupt end), which matches the report order and reasonable audible impact ranking.
judge.explains_impact: F1 explains that kick/bass 'may thin out on phones, club sub feeds' and F2 explains it 'reads as a hard cut rather than an ending' on release platforms.
judge.groups_causes: The two findings (wide low end and abrupt end) are unrelated and are correctly kept as separate priorities rather than merged.
judge.specific: The notes cite exact measurements from the report (150 Hz cutoff, 0.35 correlation, -1.06 dBTP, 0.7 dB mono loss, 0.06 dB balance) rather than generic advice.
judge.stage_appropriate: Notes reference headroom (-1.06 dBTP) and correctness of the master without penalizing loudness, consistent with a master stage.
judge.faithful: Claims track the report's measurements and findings; added phrases like 'club sub feeds' and 'phones' are reasonable elaborations of 'mono' without contradicting the report.
judge.concise: The notes add extensive extra sections (listen_for with four items, strengths with three) beyond what the two findings require, adding length without new substance.
